title: VC4Tile M4 typed verification specification
notes: M4 uses the canonical feature contract layers: dialect, invalid diagnostic, vc4tile -> ssavc4 lowered IR, ssavc4 -> scheduled vc4 artifact/resource, and hardware CPU/reference comparison when executable.
Hardware gates are the gold standard and are required for executable VC4Tile features unless a feature is strictly metadata-only and has an explicit feature_gate_contract exception.
M4 must never lower directly from vc4tile to scheduled vc4; scheduled vc4 remains the QASM-near artifact sink.
Producer adapters from Triton/IREE/MLIR gpu-like forms are future work after M4.
Text-inspection contract verifications use `inspect_files`; the verifier also accepts `files` as a backward-compatible alias so a wrong field name cannot produce files_checked=[] again.
Dialect contracts distinguish source-native ODS op definitions (`op_defs`) from assembled MLIR operation names (`assembly_ops`); comments are stripped and must not satisfy op-existence checks.
Do not add verifier-only comments/literals such as fully-qualified op names to source files. If a check would require such a comment, fix the verification contract instead.
Every implementation slice has an early build-check_vc4 and a final build-check_vc4-post so fresh artifact/hardware side effects cannot pass a slice while breaking cumulative prefix verification.
Scheduled/artifact and hardware CPU-reference contracts must force fresh candidate generation; stale .vc4_auto candidate bundles are not valid evidence.
Hardware matrix case values are exposed to runners through VC4_MATRIX_* and VC4_CASE_* environment variables.

Implementation slices run an early build-check_vc4 and a final build-check_vc4-post so fresh scheduled/artifact/hardware side effects cannot pass locally and fail only during cumulative prefix recheck.
Scheduled artifact contracts validate fresh scheduled VC4 intermediates: exactly one vc4.module, no remaining vc4tile/ssavc4 ops, and vc4.qpu.* scheduled ops before vc4-codegen.
Hardware CPU-reference contracts clean candidate/hardware state by default before running fixture phases, so stale bundles cannot satisfy fresh hardware checks.

ABI refactor gate: user/caller values are vc4tile.kernel formal args and vc4.launch_abi.args[]; program_id/block_id/warp_id are zero-operand runtime builtins and vc4.launch_abi.builtins[]; lane_id/lane_range/ssavc4.element_number are lane/register identity values outside the launch ABI.

Future ABI static-forbidden checks are intentionally required=false during ABI-1 so slices m4-00 through m4-08 do not fail solely because old source still contains stale lower ABI syntax. ABI implementation stages must turn the gate on.

M4 prefix canary: slices m4-10 and later must preserve the m4-03 minimal ABI invariant: empty/no-formal kernels lower with args=[], builtins=[], uniform_words_per_qpu=0, no synthetic total_requests/logical_request builtins, and no ssavc4.uniform.read.
